0.comment: Dori: Kaveh and the Palace of Alcazarzaray
0.content:
Dori hired the Kshahrewar architect Kaveh to build her a large, extravagant private estate and gave him a free hand on style. Kaveh did not know the famous "Lord Sangemah Bay" was Dori until they met. He persuaded her to move the site to a cliff in the northern mountains; when the work was seventy percent done, the Withering destroyed it overnight. Dori, furious, ordered him off the project and asked who would bear the losses. Kaveh sold the house his parents had left him and put in his savings to cover seventy percent, she covered the rest, and overspending left him deep in her debt. She saw he was paying for his ideals, not for her, and let him. He still pays her monthly.

Kaveh calls her shrewd and wishes she would show mercy, yet says she does not seem a bad person at heart. Dori calls him one of the few Akademiya people with dreams of his own and says she respects that. She also claims she secretly lent him a lot of Mora for the palace.

In 6.1 Nahida asked Kaveh to build the protective device for Dori's project; he worried over a dozen designs and sent it via Mehrak with a nosy letter asking about its use. Dori replied: "Let's hope there never has to be a use case."

1.content:
No one knows how Dori met the travelling mage Alice, but they are ideal partners. Alice sends inventions; Dori sells them and ships Alice's share to the safe zone nearest wherever she is, paying labour, shipping and insurance, even in advance. "I, Dori, never default on payment." On the day they met, Dori promised to be Alice's greatest business partner. Alice was her first investor. She is no longer Dori's only supplier, but her payment is always top priority.

Alice warned Dori that the world would not stay safe forever, gave her a flower-shaped pendant that stores kuuvahki for her protection, and introduced her to Skirk. In 6.1 Dori described Alice to the Traveler as "the mom of a friend of yours".

At the 6.5 Nod-Krai Trade Expo (limited event) Alice had Dori sell Hexenzirkel goods "by happiness, not by wealth", and priced an oasis-growing gemstone at "whatever keeps the kids happy". Dori grumbled, but would not break a promise to a mage, and sold it to desert children for their expo earnings.

2.comment: Dori: The Jinni in the lamp
2.content:
Dori's lamp holds a Jinni that was tricked into entering it and never left. She summons it in battle and grants its wishes afterwards; the Jinni sometimes thinks the fairy tale got things backwards. Dori's own story of how she got it: a merchant caught by a Fog Div told it of a "Genie of Beauty and Kindness" who became her supplier, and persuaded the div that it could gain the same power by entering her lamp. Asked if it is true, she charges another 990,000 Mora for "backstory details".

In Nod-Krai the kuuvahki made the Jinni faint soon after she arrived, leaving her in a life-threatening situation until Nefer rescued her.

In 6.6 she called the Jinni Plumpy, referred to it as "she", and haggled with it like a hired partner (5,000, 20,000, finally 100,000 Mora) before sending it to negotiate with Spirits of Omen. It was flung straight back. Paimon wondered how something so big fit in the lamp.

3.comment: Dori: The elder sister and the Vision
3.content:
Dori and her elder sister were inseparable, picking flowers, crossing creeks and sliding down dunes together. The elder began coughing blood. Doctors came and went; she always smiled and said she just needed rest. Dori found a crumpled prescription for herbs costing tens of millions of Mora, far beyond the family, and resolved to make a fortune so her family would never again swallow their pain behind smiles. It is implied her Vision came then. "There's nothing that Lord Sangemah Bay cannot achieve."

In 6.1 she told Nefer her sister passed away years ago, that she has been away so long she barely remembers her family's faces, and that her sister's face is fading. Her sister used to dream of a sanctuary with food, water and medicine for everyone. Dori's desert shelters and disaster stockpiles come from that dream: "I've lost family to a disaster before."

4.comment: Dori: Canned Knowledge in Port Ormos (3.0)
4.content:
In 3.0 Dori was a hidden dealer of illegal Canned Knowledge in Port Ormos, meeting only clients vetted by her informant Raunak and keeping clear of the matra. Alhaitham, blacklisted by her, sent the Traveler and Paimon as "safe" outlanders. They passed her test by outrunning the matra. She sold them capsules and an upsold "million-Mora" capsule that proved nearly worthless. Two days later she sold them intel: the Divine Knowledge Capsule had gone to Mizri, leader of Ayn Al-Ahmar, and she had photographed the deal with a Kamera. Alhaitham called it a very bold move.

Her pitch included "An Analysis of the Sociological Ideology and Dialectics of the Hilichurls" for 350,000 Mora. Her parting line: "Mora for Dori opens doors!"

5.comment: Dori: The smuggling case and the Court of Desolation (3.1)
5.content:
In Cyno's Story Quest, the Traveler kept Dori's name from Cyno, so she shared what she knew. She had quit Canned Knowledge because the smugglers flooded the market and regulations tightened. She warned of its dangers: flawed knowledge is hard to unlearn, and overuse dulls thinking. She guessed the smuggling was a cover for an auction tied to the Court of Desolation, then sold a "Limited Edition Desert Travel Kit" with a map to it and billed the expense to Cyno.

Per the wiki storyline, her associate later tried to collect from Cyno, who knew nothing of the debt and arrested him for disturbing the peace.

6.content: In Kaveh's Hangout Event, Kaveh and the Traveler asked her for introductions to sponsors for a library for desert children. She demanded 500,000 Mora, waived it when Kaveh pleaded, and introduced three partners who declined. Then she revealed herself as "the most famous merchant in Sumeru" and agreed to fund the whole complex. Through a long pause and a "menacing" look she let Kaveh volunteer to waive his commission. She then revealed she owned all the land around Aaru Village. Kaveh still thanked her and apologised for calling her Mora-obsessed; she paid for dinner.

7.comment: Dori: Nefer and the Curatorium of Secrets
7.content:
Nefer, a fellow Sumeran and boss of the Curatorium of Secrets in Nod-Krai, rescued Dori when the kuuvahki knocked out her Jinni. Dori gave her thirty percent off everything ever since. She first warned the Traveler away from the Curatorium as a ruinously expensive rival with a temper; she later admitted she simply resented not having Nefer in her debt. Nefer reads her motives effortlessly, which unsettles her.

In 6.1 Nefer borrowed Alice's pendant from Dori and drained it in the fight with Rerir; Dori was outraged but let it go as repayment. Afterwards Nefer revealed she knew about Dori's shelters and land purchases, and the two talked about home and lost family. In 6.6 Nefer told Candace and Dehya, and Dori accused her of trading her secret for sympathy.

In a 6.0 anecdote Dori bought Nefer pricey Sumeran wine to pave the way for a deal, while Nefer planned to take a cut. Dori said she would never leave her "card table", Sumeru, or she would be left with nothing.

8.comment: Dori: Rerir, the pendant and the device (6.1)
8.content: In 6.1 Jahoda dragged a sleepy Dori to the Curatorium. Nefer, preparing for an enemy "with the power to bring a nation to its knees", borrowed her flower-shaped pendant from Alice; Dori allowed three days and threatened a million Mora per extra hour. Nefer used up all its kuuvahki. Dori then joined the plan, saying she was doing someone a favour and protecting her Nod-Krai business. She supplied a device built by Kaveh for Nahida's secret project, which the Traveler carried to Albedo on Hiisi Island and which helped in the battle. Afterward she bought the Traveler's drinks.

9.content: In 6.2 Dori ran a Moon-Prayer Night ring-toss stall in Nasha Town staffed by fairy-tale origami and clockwork folk. Columbina played a free round, and Durin and the Wanderer stopped by. Her "employees" leapt into the rings for Durin and he won the grand prize, a Dodoco Alice, then gave it to a child. Dori despaired at "bleeding hearts" ruining her business. She planned to rebox Columbina's Moon-Prayer Candy as "blessed by the Moon Goddess" and have her assistant Urwa sell it.

10.comment: Dori: The Irminsul crisis in Sumeru (6.6)
10.content:
In 6.6, after Collei's premonitory dream, Nahida evacuated the rainforest to Caravan Ribat and requisitioned Dori's whole Sumpter Beast Park. Dori held the line near Aaru Village with Tighnari and Collei against Spirits of Omen, spending twelve rare items. In the plan to repair Irminsul she ran the elemental energy amplifier, with Faruzan, Collei and Nicole supporting her, inside the Mausoleum of King Deshret. She said the Akademiya paid most of it and she gave "a small token", lamenting that some crises cannot even be profited from.

The night before the battle she gave Dehya free perfume because Dehya and Candace had rescued her caravan, and was mortified to learn Nefer had told them about her shelters. She told Candace that being able to get angry shows you are in touch with the world. After the crisis she was already eyeing trade in local Sumpter Beasts and imported goods, sulking at Nefer about her lost "mercantile majesty".

11.content: Dori avoids the Akademiya because its rules make business "nearly impossible" and most of her wares break them. She once caught Alhaitham asking her staff questions and calls Akademiya people pig-headed and dishonest. Alhaitham calls her sharp and self-reliant, a woman who makes her dreams real; he does not condone her actions but appreciates her attitude to life. The Kshahrewar are her exception: they signed a private contract with her, her Mora for their technology.

12.content: Alice introduced Skirk to Dori. Skirk sells her rare monster parts because she needs Mora to get by, and likes that Dori never asks about her past. In a 6.0 anecdote in Nasha Town Dori paid six million Mora for Radiant Exoskeletons; Skirk took half in cash and had the rest given to the Traveler as supplies. Dori calls her the perfect customer, quality goods and no haggling, and Skirk disappears through a rift as usual.

13.content: Dori's caravans use Sumpter Beasts, so she built them an "amusement park", feeds them the best food and checks their health. She then opened it to tourists, selling tickets, food and souvenirs until it paid for the beasts' upkeep. Her love for them is genuine, and so is her plan to profit from it. She will show visitors her Sumpter Beasts, for a fee. In 6.6 the whole park was requisitioned for Sumeru's evacuation.

14.comment: Dori: Dori in festivals and events
14.content: Limited-time event appearances, canon but not universally known. Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2): she handed the Traveler suspicious schematics linked to the Nilotpala Cup tournament (per the wiki storyline). A Parade of Providence (3.6): she set up stalls at the Interdarshan Championship and was incensed when Kaveh smashed the Diadem of Knowledge she had hoped to buy cheap and resell. Lantern Rite (4.4): with Layla and Faruzan testing her new Fontaine ship, she tried to dodge paying for a 30,000-Mora dish at Wangshu Inn. Summertide Scales and Tales (4.8): she lent out a borrowed mystery novel for fees until Cyno noticed its return date. Chromatic Ode (5.1): Candace bargained her down to 30,000 Mora for intel. Where Waves Meet the Reef (6.5): the Nod-Krai Trade Expo, where she sold Alice's oasis gemstone to desert children.
